advances: Failure of one prescribed disjoint-reflected-pair lower certificate on an actual (n,d)=(1,4) body. The same body satisfies the stronger Γ₄/2 depth target by a different all-cap argument.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The fiber description follows by fixing $z$ in the defining inequalities; the defining functions give convexity and the section at zero has positive interior. The nonempty integer bases are exactly $-16,\ldots,16$, and $M/V=1+2\sum_{k=1}^{16}(1-k/17)^4=571217/83521$. Both $r_z$ and $c_z$ interpolate affinely on the two sides of zero, so the entire body is also the convex hull of these actual integer fibers.

For each pair write $\theta=\gamma_K(y-m_{k,h})/\rho_{k,h}$. If $\theta\ge1$ its credit is zero. Otherwise choose $w\in K$ with $y-m_{k,h}=\theta\rho_{k,h} w$ (use $w=0$ if $\theta=0$). In each endpoint $c_i+r_iK$ the copy centered at $c_i+\theta r_iw$ with radius $(1-\theta)r_i$ is contained by convexity. The two copy centers average to $y$. After moving the containing halfspace to pass through the mark, the centered continuous thresholds in the two endpoint copies are opposite. By e561372a5640eef8 and homogeneity, their captured total is at least $V(1-\theta)^4\Phi_4(r_{k-h},r_{k+h})$. A purely base-normal cap contains at least one full copy and gives the same lower bound, since $\Phi_4(r,s)\le\min(r,s)^4$. These disjoint pairs are separate from the own-fiber term, which pays at least $p_{K_k}(y)$ even when its trace is full.

Reflect the base to assume $k\ge0$. The pair range is $1\le h\le16-k$, and the identity $|k-h|+|k+h|=2\max(k,h)$ gives $m_{k,h}=\max(k,h)v/17$ and $\rho_{k,h}=1-\max(k,h)/17$. Average the four continuous coordinates of $y$ over their permutations to obtain $xv$ in $K_k$. The pair centers are invariant and the gauge is convex and invariant, so every pair gauge decreases. On this axis $\gamma_K(av)=a$ for $a\ge0$ and $-4a$ for $a\le0$, as follows from the simplex inequalities. If $x<k/17$, moving the averaged point to $c_k$ further decreases all gauges. Also $p_{K_k}(y)\le\Gamma_4Vr_k^4=p_{K_k}(c_k)$: the largest barycentric coordinate of a point is at least $1/5$, and its through-point vertex cap has fraction $(1-\lambda)^4$ for that coordinate $\lambda$. At the centroid the matching lower bound is the full-volume case of 6769574fc1bd9f8d.

For $x\ge k/17$ the barycentric coordinate at the vertex $v$ equals $(1+4(x-k/17)/r_k)/5$ at both $y$ and $xv$, since this coordinate is unchanged by permutation averaging. The vertex cap bounds the own depth above by $\Gamma_4 V(1-x)^4$. The copy $xv+(1-x)K\subseteq K_k$, obtained by convex interpolation toward $v$, has centroid $xv$ and gives the same lower bound there. At $x=1$ the bound and depth are zero. Thus we may take an axis point with $k/17\le x\le1$ without decreasing the certificate.

More generally the coefficient from e561372a5640eef8 satisfies $\Phi_d(r,s)\le2\Gamma_d((r+s)/2)^d$ for all $d\ge1$ and $r,s>0$. For $d=1$ it says $\min(r,s)\le(r+s)/2$. Otherwise order $r\le s$ and put $c_d=(2\Gamma_d)^{1/d}\ge2/(d+1)$. In the interpolation branch, $(1-c_d)/(d-1)\le c_d/2$ bounds the linear bracket by $c_d(r+s)/2$. In the plateau branch $s\ge dr$ implies $r\le c_d(r+s)/2$. This comparison concerns the certificate coefficient. Consequently the noncentral $h$ term is bounded by $2\Gamma_4 V(\rho_{k,h}-\gamma_K(xv-m_{k,h}))_+^4$. For $h>k$ this is exactly the central $h$ term at $xv$, where the endpoint radii agree. For $h\le k$ both this expression and the central $h$ term equal $2\Gamma_4 V(1-x)^4$, since $x\ge k/17$. The own term is also the same as centrally, and every extra central term is nonnegative. It suffices to maximize the central certificate.

At $k=0$, divided by $\Gamma_4V$, the own term is $(1-x)^4$. Each central pair contributes $2(1-x)^4$ for $h/17\le x$, or $2(1-5h/17+4x)_+^4$ for $h/17\ge x$. The two formulas agree at $x=h/17$. On every interval between successive $j/17$ the sum is convex, so its maximum occurs at a listed endpoint. The numerator at $x=j/17$ in units $17^{-4}$ is
$$
 (2j+1)(17-j)^4+2\sum_{h=j+1}^{16}(17-5h+4j)_+^4,\qquad j=0,\ldots,17.
$$
In order these are $129827,228484,274375,282546,265403,232930,192927,151250,112049,77986,50453,29810,15625,6912,2349,496,33,0$. The largest is at $j=3$, and $571217-2\cdot282546=6125$.

For the actual-depth comparison scale only the base by $u=z/17$ and write $a=1/17$. The resulting ordinary five-body $Q$ has sections $(1-|u|)T$ for $|u|\le16/17$. Its volume is $V W$, $W=2(1-a^5)/5$; its centroid has zero base by reflection and each other coordinate is $(1-a^6)/[6(1-a^5)]$ by integrating the scaled fiber centroids against the fourth powers of their radii. This point lies in the actual sampled central fiber since each coordinate is positive and their sum is less than one. Ordinary five-dimensional Grünbaum, the full-volume case of 6769574fc1bd9f8d, bounds each containing closed cap by $\Gamma_5WV$ from below. Apply ae8f94d7d0e2ab8a with $s=4$, grid $a\mathbb Z$, and peak section volume $V$. The $a$-weighted sampled mass of every such cap is at least $V(\Gamma_5W-a)$, including pure base-normal caps. The sampled total is $aM=33601V/83521$. The ratio is $35167522/138805731$; the unnormalized gap in units of $V$ after weighting is $\Gamma_5W-a-(128/625)aM/V=4212567682/215640781875>0$. The invertible base rescaling identifies these normalized cap masses with the original ones.

statement:
Let $T=\{X\in\mathbb R^4:X_i\ge0,\ \sum_iX_i\le1\}$, $V=|T|=1/24$, $g=(1/5,1/5,1/5,1/5)$, $K=T-g$ and $v=-g$. The convex polytope
$$
 C=\{(z,X): |z|\le16,\ X_i\ge0,\ \textstyle\sum_iX_i+|z|/17\le1\}
$$
has exactly 33 positive integer fibers. In coordinates $x=X-g$ they are $K_k=c_k+r_kK$, $r_k=1-|k|/17$, $c_k=|k|v/17$. Its total mixed four-volume is $M=571217V/83521$.

Let $p_{K_k}(y)$ denote ordinary raw closed-halfspace depth, $\gamma_K$ the Minkowski gauge of $K$, and $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. For $0<r\le s$, define $\Phi_4(r,s)=[r c+(s-r)(1-c)/3]^4$ for $s\le4r$ and $\Phi_4(r,s)=r^4$ for $s\ge4r$, where $c=(2\Gamma_4)^{1/4}$; extend symmetrically. For each integer anchor $k$ and every $y\in K_k$ consider
$$
 L_k(y)=p_{K_k}(y)+V\sum_h
 \left(1-\frac{\gamma_K(y-m_{k,h})}{\rho_{k,h}}\right)_+^4
 \Phi_4(r_{k-h},r_{k+h}),
 \quad m_{k,h}=\frac{c_{k-h}+c_{k+h}}2,\quad
 \rho_{k,h}=\frac{r_{k-h}+r_{k+h}}2.
$$
The sum uses all positive integers $h$ with both endpoints in $[-16,16]$. Every closed cap containing $(k,y)$ has raw mixed mass at least $L_k(y)$, but
$$
 \max_{k\in[-16,16]\cap\mathbb Z,\ y\in K_k} L_k(y)
 =\Gamma_4 V\,\frac{282546}{83521}
 =\frac{\Gamma_4 M}{2}-\Gamma_4 V\,\frac{6125}{167042},
$$
attained at $k=0$, $y=3v/17$. In original coordinates the actual point at base zero with $X_i=(1-17^{-6})/[6(1-17^{-5})]$ has normalized mixed depth at least $35167522/138805731>128/625=\Gamma_4/2$.
title: Exact all-anchor shortfall of a reflected-pair gauge certificate
